5. Layout and Density

Space

Space is a 4-pixel scale with two half steps: 2, 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64 and 96 pixels, --nc-space-1 to --nc-space-10, and --nc-space-0. A part's padding and the gap between parts take a step of the scale; a value between two steps is a sign that a part is the wrong size.

Controls

HeightTokenWhere
28 px--nc-control-smA ghost key repeated in every row of a table, a key on a screen
36 px--nc-control-mdEvery key and field of the interface
44 px--nc-control-lgEvery control on a phone, and the primary key of a sign-in card

A key stands --nc-travel, 2 pixels, proud of its plate. A table row is 40 pixels high and its head 36.

Long-Form Pages

Documentation is set to be scanned: a reader comes for one answer and finds it by the page around it. Text runs on a 42 rem measure, --nc-measure, at 15 pixels with a line height of 1.6, the reading role: about 95 characters to a line. On a phone it is 16 pixels. The title is 32 pixels, title-long, a section heading 24, heading-long, and the first paragraph 18, lead, at every width. A section starts with a rule, 40 pixels after the text before it and 32 before its heading. Listings and tables start --nc-bleed, 20 pixels, before the text and use the width of the sheet, so what is in them lines up with the text: a sheet 52 rem wide inside its padding holds a listing line of 100 characters.

The selector, the sheet and the page index stand together in the middle of the window and are no wider than 90 rem together. On a wider window the rest is margin on both sides, so the page index stays beside the text it indexes. The selector and the page index are set at 13 pixels, and an entry of the selector is 28 pixels high, --nc-control-sm.

Landing and Product Pages

The one headline is 60 pixels, the headline role, 48 at 1088 pixels and below and 40 on a phone. Keep it to what two lines hold beside the instrument. The line under it is 18 pixels on a measure of 36 rem. The keys are the interface's, 36 pixels, and 44 on a phone: a landing page is read at a desk like the documentation it leads to.

The Console

The console is a faceplate. A sticky bar holds the brand, the way out of the boundary and the display; below it the workspace stands between the braces of the boundary the user acts in, with the selector on a plate that runs the workspace's height. A table's unused rows keep the row rhythm, ruled but empty.

Breakpoints

Media queries cannot read custom properties, so css/base.css repeats these numbers, and tokens/tokens.mjs and mui/instrument.json export them for a theme's breakpoints.

At and belowTokenWhat changes
1280 px--nc-breakpoint-deskDocumentation drops its page index
1088 px--nc-breakpoint-tabletThe console's selector, the way out and the session move into a sheet
640 px--nc-breakpoint-phoneA table becomes a list of two-line rows, a dialog becomes a sheet that rises from the bottom edge with its keys side by side, and every control is at least 44 pixels high

No page scrolls sideways at any width: a listing scrolls inside its own screen. The one exception is the kit's catalog, specimens/foundations.html, which is laid out for a desktop window. A table that becomes a list keeps its table roles in the markup, so assistive technology still reads a table.
